items.title: Too important to hold to account
items.body: Both commentators make the same uncomfortable observation: a leader was restored because the organisation could not be seen to manage without him, and the conduct towards staff was set aside. The NHS has its own history of this, from surgeons to chief executives. Freedom to Speak Up exists because performance was allowed to outweigh behaviour. The lesson is not about chips. Nobody should be too valuable to be subject to the rules.

items.title: Reinstated before the investigation reported
items.body: The board's inquiry is unfinished, and he is back in post. In clinical governance we would call that prejudging the outcome. NLW notes the non-cynical reading, that the accusations may not stand; Zitron assumes they do. Neither knows. An investigation only has value if its result could have gone either way.

items.title: Little clinical relevance; the supply chain is steadier for now
items.body: Practically, the scenario in which Nvidia stopped supporting smaller AI firms has receded, so the near-term risk to suppliers of NHS tools is lower than it looked a fortnight ago. Zitron argues this only postpones the reckoning. The earlier advice stands either way: know where a tool is hosted, and keep contracts short enough to leave.
